summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic intestinal dysmotility, and a long-standing femoral central venous catheter presented with fevers during an outpatient iron infusion. She was found to have a coagulase-negative staphylococcal bloodstream infection likely originating from her central line. Initial management included IV vancomycin and monitoring, but the catheter developed a mechanical leak despite a bedside repair. Due to ongoing infection risk and device failure, the catheter was replaced via interventional radiology. She received a full course of IV antibiotics, completed her iron infusion, and remained stable throughout. She was discharged home with plans for continued IV vancomycin, vancomycin-heparin locks, and home nursing support, with follow-up arranged.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter, initial encounter
Breakdown (mechanical) of infusion catheter, initial encounter
Leakage of infusion catheter, initial encounter
Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
